title: Diameter of a binary tree
label: single
statement: Return the **diameter** of a binary tree: the number of **edges** on the longest path between any two nodes. The path does not have to pass through the root.
provenance: In your recent LinkedIn list (Oct 2026). LeetCode 543. Agoda's tree-diameter question in this bank is the general-tree version (edges list).

sources.name: Your list of recently asked LinkedIn coding questions (supplied 26 Oct 2026)

stages.title: The diameter
stages.say: Return the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.
stages.require: Implement `BinaryDiameter.Of(root)`. Empty or single node → 0. Must survive a 100,000-deep tree.

1.a: Edges here; nodes would be one more.
Not necessarily — the classic wrong answer only checks the root.

2.a: O(n) time, O(n) for the heights and stack.

2.q: Why is "height at every node" O(n²)?
2.a: Each height call walks the whole subtree; on a chain that is n + (n−1) + …

4.q: A general tree given as edges.
4.a: Two BFS passes: the farthest node from anywhere is one end of a diameter — the Agoda question in this bank.

5.a: Longest univalue path and binary tree maximum path sum use the same "best bend at each node" idea.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Return the **diameter** of a binary tree: the number of **edges** on the longest path between any two nodes. The path does not have to pass through the root.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Edges or nodes? (Edges.)
- Must it pass through the root? (No.)
- How deep can it be? (Deep — avoid recursion, or say the limit.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Every path has a single highest node where it bends. At that node its length is (height of left subtree) + (height of right subtree). So compute heights bottom-up and keep the best sum — one pass.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Only checking the path through the root.
- Calling a separate height function at every node — O(n²).
- Counting nodes instead of edges.
- Recursion on a 100,000-deep chain.
